details:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten: Echoes of Cosmic Exploration

What does the project do and how does it work?

Abandoned But Not Forgotten: Echoes of Cosmic Exploration is an interactive, visual-novel-style cosmic archive that brings the stories of four remarkable space missions back to life.

The project takes users on a journey through a futuristic digital archive, where they can explore four mission records:

  • Surveyor Landers (Moon): Pioneering robotic lunar landings and helping prepare for human exploration.
  • Apollo Lunar Module (Moon): Enabling astronauts to land on the Moon and return to lunar orbit.
  • Spirit and Opportunity (Mars): Exploring Martian geology and discovering evidence of ancient water.
  • Ingenuity (Mars): Demonstrating the possibility of powered, controlled flight on another planet.

Each mission has an introductory storytelling section followed by a detailed mission file containing its objectives, discoveries, scientific contributions, achievements and final status. Clickable navigation allows users to move between the archive directory and individual mission records.

What benefits does it have?

The project makes space exploration history easier and more engaging to discover. It brings together information about missions whose operational journeys have ended but whose scientific and technological contributions are worthy of remembering.

By presenting information through short narratives, organized mission records and interactive navigation, it aims to make space history more approachable for students, young space enthusiasts and general audiences.

What is the intended impact?

Our aim is to provide knowledge of past space missions and inspire curiosity about planetary exploration.

We want users to understand that even when a spacecraft stops operating, the knowledge it gathered and the possibilities it created continue to influence future exploration.

The project also encourages interest in space science, engineering, robotics and the history of human exploration beyond Earth.

What tools and technologies were used?

  • Canva: Used to design the presentation, create the futuristic archive interface and build clickable navigation between slides.
  • ChatGPT (OpenAI): Used as an AI-assisted tool for drafting, organising and refining presentation content.

The current prototype is a Canva-based interactive presentation. It does not use custom programming languages or dedicated hardware.

How is the project creative?

Instead of presenting mission information as a conventional slideshow or a list of historical facts, we transformed it into a fictional cosmic archive.

A mission-control-style narrative guides users through the experience, while each mission is presented as an individual archive record. The futuristic visual design, cinematic introductions and clickable navigation create the feeling of exploring a digital collection of forgotten missions.

The storytelling approach connects scientific achievements with the human curiosity and technological progress behind space exploration.

What factors did we consider?

While developing the project, we considered:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using NASA mission records and official mission resources to research objectives, discoveries, timelines and final statuses.
  • Educational value: Presenting meaningful scientific and historical information in an understandable format.
  • User experience: Keeping the archive organised and providing clear navigation between mission records.
  • Visual consistency: Maintaining a futuristic space-archive atmosphere throughout the experience.
  • Historical significance: Highlighting not only what each mission achieved, but also how its contributions continue beyond the end of its operation.
  • Accessibility: Keeping the experience simple to navigate and understandable for audiences with different levels of space-science knowledge.

NASA Data and Resources

NASA's National Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), along with NASA mission archives and official mission pages, served as research resources for the mission records. Information about mission objectives, historical timelines, scientific findings and final mission statuses was used to develop the four profiles.

All referenced data sources, images and supporting tools are acknowledged in the project's references section.
